messages:
alexa: opened PR to fix /embeddings docs. example used `input` as a string but OpenAPI and runtime expect `inputs: [string]`. Also found mismatch in response: docs showed `vector: [float32]` but runtime returns float64 and vectors are 1536 not 1024. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/711
omar: ugh that explains a bunch of user reports. can we add both forms (single-string shorthand + explicit array) and a tiny migration note about vector length + precision?
li: agree. also saw the Rust SDK snippet uses `Vec<f32>` which will truncate; change to `Vec<f64>` and add a decode-tolerant example. I'll add a short Rust fragment:
```rust
let mut v: Vec<f64> = serde_json::from_slice(&body)?;
```
alexa: pushed changes: examples now show `inputs: ["a","b"]` and `input: "a" // shorthand`, updated response sample to `embedding: [0.123456789, ...]` with length 1536 and note about double precision. adjusted OpenAPI schema to `type: array, items: {type: number, format: double}`.
ci-bot: PR #711 updated by alexa (docs) - CI: docs build running
sam: nit: the example curl had `Accept: application/json; charset=utf-8` which caused some clients to mis-handle numbers. prefer plain `Accept: application/json`. Also add a quick test assertion in the examples folder that checks vector length so CI can catch regressions.
alexa: added test assertion `assert_eq!(embedding.len(), 1536);` to examples/tests and removed charset from Accept. CI green. leaving a short migration note: "If your client used f32 or assumed 1024 dims, update to f64 and 1536 dims; library adapters will accept older shapes for 30 days."
omar: thanks. LGTM. merging after squash.
